subject: MediQX — post-demo technical + commercial summary and quantization playbook
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Carl Hansen <carl.hansen@mediqx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 15:18:00 +0000
Subject: MediQX demo follow-up — recommended models, benchmarks, and next steps

Hi Carl —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so your team has a clear path for evaluation and procurement: 

Summary of technical fit
- Primary workload: clinical note summarization + multi-field extraction (avg doc length ~900 tokens, 95th percentile ~1,600).
- Latency requirement: 95th percentile < 450ms for interactive workflows.
- Quality bar: extract accuracy > 92% on key fields (diagnosis, meds).

Recommended model candidates (for initial eval)
1) Llama-2-Chat-13B (FP16 baseline) — strong baseline for quality, predictable cost.
2) RedCloud-7B-AWQ — best throughput at 4-bit AWQ with modest quality delta; recommended if throughput/cost dominates.
3) Falcon-40B-GPTQ (8-bit mixed) — high quality for edge cases but heavier infra.

Quantization/throughput playbook (short)
- Start with FP16 or FP8 (if you have constrained VRAM but want minimal quality risk).
- AWQ 4-bit: gives biggest cost win, often with 2–4% metric drop on extraction tasks; run on a held-out prompt set first.
- GPTQ 4/8-bit: middle ground; generally better quality than AWQ at slightly higher latency.

Links & artifacts attached
- promptset_mediqx_v1.jsonl — canonical call-and-response prompts plus 150 labeled examples we discussed.
- mediqx_benchmark_links.txt — precomputed perf/latency charts and token-cost estimates per model/format.
- quant_tradeoffs_onepager.pdf — visual tradeoffs table (AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8).

Immediate next steps
1) We propose a 2-week scoped pilot: 150 labeled examples (you provide labels or we can help) + batch of 10k live inference tokens to validate latency/cost.
2) We can run AWQ and GPTQ runs on your sample set and provide delta matrices (quality vs latency) within 5 business days after sample receipt.
3) Commercial: if throughput numbers look good, we’ll provide a Dedicated capacity estimate and an initial reserved commit proposal.

Action items for your team
- Please share the finalized 150-label set (or confirm we should use the attached promptset_mediqx_v1).
- Put procurement on copy if you want pricing draft: procurement@mediqx.com.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute technical deep-dive with your ML infra person next week — Marissa and Ben will run the bench.

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer

1) On AWQ vs GPTQ: how often do you see AWQ failures on extraction boundaries (e.g., splitting 'dosage' into multiple tokens)? We need to avoid silent omissions in medication fields.
2) For FP8 — we don’t have infra ready for it yet. If we start with FP16 and then move to AWQ, what is the typical engineering lift?
3) Commercial: procurement wants a ballpark for a 3-month pilot (50k token/day average). Can you provide a cost estimate range and any potential credits?

Also looping procurement so they see the recommended pilot. We’ll aim to share the labeled set by EOD Friday if possible.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: MediQX demo follow-up — recommended models, benchmarks, and next steps

Carl — great questions, answered inline below. Marissa and Ben are copied for the bench runs and commercial follow-up.

1) AWQ extraction risk
- Observed failure mode: AWQ can occasionally truncate or split tokenization boundaries that impact short, numeric fields (dosage, frequency). In our internal tests on a similar dataset we saw ~3% field-level drop relative to FP16 for medication dosage; important to measure on your labeled set.
- Mitigation: conservative post-processing (regex normalization), prompt engineering to force canonical formats, and hybrid routing (use AWQ for high-throughput cases and FP16 fallback for low-confidence outputs). We will provide a per-field confusion matrix.

2) Engineering lift FP16 -> AWQ
- If you use Redwood Dedicated or Hosted, we handle model conversion and runtime bitswitching; customer engineering effort is minimal (primarily validating outputs and integrating fallback logic).
- On-prem: you'll need a short runtime integration (1–2 engineer-days) to add the AWQ runtime artifact and test.

3) Pilot cost estimate (3 months, 50k tokens/day avg)
- FP16 baseline (Redwood hosted): ~$4k–$6k/month (tokens + baseline infra).
- AWQ 4-bit (Redwood Dedicated burst): ~$1.6k–$2.4k/month (significant cost reduction).
- We can offer a pilot credit of $3,000 toward first month of Dedicated if we sign an SOW within 30 days. 

Next steps we propose
- You: confirm whether you want Redwood to label the 150 items or if you’ll provide them (status by Fri).
- Us: Marissa will produce AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP16 delta matrices on your sample set within 5 business days of receiving the labeled prompts. Ben will draft a commercial pilot estimate and SOW template.

We’ll attach an explicit run plan and the delta-matrix template to the HubSpot deal.

Warmly,
Karthik
